records.name: Cauca
records.summary:
For Cauca the audited record carries no regional statute, enforcement practice or incident specific to trans visitors, so the national baseline stands: an August 2025 investigation documents continuing killings of queer and trans people — gangs linked to queer and trans deaths after a viral torture-murder of a trans woman that year — and a 2024 national report records armed groups in Cauca's larger region circulating "social cleansing" flyers giving trans women ultimatums to leave or be killed, amid 41 recorded killings of trans women in 2023.

Armed-group presence is strong in Cauca's countryside nationally, but no source on this record ties that to trans-specific local mechanisms; the file deliberately stops at the national pattern.

records.name: Huila
records.summary:
Huila's file previously carried only methodology boilerplate about being assessed at the national position; stripped of that, the sourced reality is national: continuing killings of queer and trans people reported in an August 2025 investigation — in parts of the country, being queer means "to sign your own death sentence" — and a 2024 report of armed groups circulating "social cleansing" threats against trans women, with 41 trans women killed nationally in 2023 and more the following spring.

No Huila-specific statute, incident or protection mechanism appears in the audited sources. What a visitor can plan on is the national pattern of high lethality and near-total impunity; nothing on this record marks Huila as better or worse than that baseline.
